title: AI crawler registry
description: Schema for crawlers.json — a sourced registry of AI crawler user-agent tokens and, crucially, what blocking each one actually costs you. Blocking a search crawler removes you from AI answers; blocking a training crawler does not. Most published robots.txt advice conflates the two.

enums.description: Human-readable glossary of the allowed purpose and blocking_effect values.

token.description: The exact user-agent token as written in a robots.txt User-agent line. Case-insensitive when matching, but reproduced here as the vendor documents it.

product.description: The surface this crawler feeds, e.g. 'ChatGPT search' or 'foundation model training'.

blocking_effect.description: The actionable field. This is what actually happens to you if you Disallow this token.

respects_robots_txt.description: False where the vendor states robots.txt may be bypassed or ignored, which is typical for user-initiated fetches.

source_quote.description: The vendor's own wording. Entries without this MUST carry a `verification` flag rather than implying a first-party source.

verified.description: When this entry was last checked against its source. A token's classification can change; treat an old date as a hypothesis.

verification.description: Present only when no first-party quote could be obtained. Its presence is the honest signal that the entry is weaker than the others.

allOf.$comment: Integrity rule: every entry is either quoted from the vendor or explicitly flagged as unverified. Nothing is allowed to look sourced when it isn't.
